unconditionalNewFacts: R(3,k) <= k^2 for EVERY k (R_three_le_sq) - the first upper bound on R(3,.) in this campaign, with no hypotheses at all. Proved by running Shearer's own skeleton at the trivial independence input 1/(D+1): in a triangle-free graph with no independent k-set every neighbourhood is independent (indep_neighborhood) hence has fewer than k vertices, so greedy extraction (exists_indep_of_cover) yields an independent set of size >= n/k, which is also below k, so n < k^2.

R(3,3) = 6 EXACTLY (R_three_three_eq_six). Attack01 recorded the upper half as OBSTRUCTION 5, 'not attempted', noting `decide` is unavailable. It needs no search: if neither G nor its complement has a triangle then each of the two neighbourhoods of a fixed vertex is an independent set of the other graph, so each has at most 2 elements - but together they partition the other 5 vertices.

(RamseySet 3 k).Nonempty for EVERY k (RamseySet_three_nonempty) - Ramsey's theorem for s=3, which Mathlib does not have, follows from R(3,k) <= k^2. This DISCHARGES Attack01's OBSTRUCTION 4: the five Attack01 statements that carried nonemptiness as a hypothesis are restated here unconditionally (R_three_le_iff, lt_R_of_witness_uncond, le_R_three, R_three_mem_Icc, lower_bound_of_witness_family_uncond).
The two-sided sandwich (log x - 1)/(x-1) < shearerF x < log x/(x-1) for x > 1 (shearerF_sandwich), pinning Shearer's f(x) ~ log x / x with no asymptotic machinery - only log x < x - 1 and log x > 0.

1/(x+1) < shearerF x for x > exp 2 (carowei_lt_shearerF): Shearer's independence input STRICTLY beats the Caro-Wei input that the unconditional R(3,k) <= k^2 was built from. This is the exact formal sense in which Shearer's theorem improves the bound, and it is the only part of that improvement provable without Shearer's inequality itself.

shearer_estimate: for every eps > 0, eventually there is an integer n with k <= n*f(k-1) and n <= (1+eps)*k^2/log k. Proved, not assumed. Mentions no graph and no Ramsey number. Witness n = ceil(k/f(k-1)); driven by the sandwich above plus log(k-1) >= log k - log 2.

obstructionDelta.OBSTRUCTION 2 (Shearer upper bound): REDUCED, NOT CLOSED. Attack01 carried the whole asymptotic R(3,k) <= (1+o(1))k^2/log k as one opaque hypothesis. Attack02 splits it into (i) ShearerBound - Shearer's FINITE independence inequality in max-degree form - and (ii) an elementary calculus estimate about f and log alone; (ii) is PROVED (shearer_estimate) and the deduction (i) -> asymptotic bound is PROVED (shearer_upper_of_bound, no second hypothesis). The residue is therefore exactly ShearerBound: one 1983 combinatorial inequality.
obstructionDelta.OBSTRUCTION 3 (HHKP lower bound c >= 1/2: UNCHANGED, open. Still unformalized. lower_bound_of_witness_family_uncond now types it as a pure construction problem with NO side conditions at all (the Ramsey hypothesis is gone).

NOT ATTEMPTED: monotonicity (antitonicity) of shearerF, which is what converts Shearer's average-degree statement into the max-degree form used by ShearerBound. Carried inside the ShearerBound hypothesis rather than proved.
calibration: Shearer's upper bound R(3,k) <= (1+o(1))k^2/log k is PUBLISHED (J. B. Shearer, 'A note on the independence number of triangle-free graphs', Discrete Math. 46 (1983) 83-87). R(3,3) = 6 is textbook. R(3,k) = O(k^2) is Erdos-Szekeres-era. NOVELTY IS DEAD ON ALL OF IT - exactly as with #503. What is new is that these are now machine-checked against the frozen spec's own definition of R, with clean triples, and that the unformalized residue of the constant-1 upper bound has been narrowed to a single finite inequality.
